title: Tenant system tool catalog pagination and governed chunk continuation

phases.objective: Prove that an authenticated tenant can enumerate the complete visible system-tool catalog through bounded cursor pages and governed response chunks without fallback search, cross-tenant chunk access, duplicate tools, or leakage of admin/blocked tools.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: GET /system/tools with bounded limit and response budget
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: All tenant-visible tools are enumerated through catalog next_cursor and response_chunk_read until completion, while a second tenant cannot read the first tenant's chunk and admin-only tools remain absent from every tenant page.
steps: Mount the production System Layer router with a bounded User-JWT-shaped tenant principal and process-local fake DB pool.
Request /system/tools with a small catalog limit and governed response budget so the real response chunk shield is exercised.
Attempt the returned chunk continuation from a different tenant and verify fail-closed response_chunk_not_found.
Use /system/tools/call with response_chunk_read to reconstruct each tenant catalog page before following the catalog next_cursor.
Continue until the catalog reports page.has_more=false without switching to any fallback discovery surface.
Verify no duplicate tool names and no blocked/admin-only tool names appear on any tenant page.
Read the admin catalog separately and prove runtime_endpoint_call remains available there while absent from the tenant traversal.
assertions: The initial bounded /system/tools response is governed-response chunked and exposes chunk_id plus a continuation cursor.
response_chunk_read is usable through the production /system/tools/call surface until each serialized catalog page is complete.
Chunk ownership is tenant scoped; another tenant receives response_chunk_not_found.
Catalog next_cursor traverses more than one bounded page and terminates with page.has_more=false.
Tenant-blocked and admin-only system tools remain absent across every page, including later pages.
An admin-only reference tool remains present in the admin catalog, proving filtering rather than global removal.
No live database, provider, connector, credential, Production, or mutation action occurs.
